items.title: Footer link `Store locator` opens the store locator with the heading and all four stores in order
covers: Outputs: footer link Store locator opens /stores
Outputs: heading Store locator
Outputs: store table (order, name, address, city, hours)
AC1
items.reason: AC1 is the entry point of the whole feature: the footer link, the `/stores` route, the heading and the fixed store list with exact text and order. A wrong href, a reordered array or a typo in an address or in the en-dash hours would all break it. It needs the real layout (footer) and routing, so it is an e2e case on the test stack.

items.title: Footer link `Store locator` on a catalog item page also opens `/stores`
covers: AC1: Given a shopper on any page
Outputs: footer link Store locator opens /stores
items.reason: AC1 says "on any page"; the footer href is relative (`stores`), so on a nested route such as `/item/99` a wrong base resolution would land on `/item/stores`. A second starting page catches that. e2e because it depends on the rendered layout and the base href.

items.title: Typing `red` in City and pressing Find stores lists only AdventureWorks Redmond and puts `city=red` in the URL
covers: AC2
Inputs: City prefix filter, case-insensitive
Outputs: Find stores puts ?city=<text> in URL
items.reason: AC2 checks the form round trip: the `City` text box, the `Find stores` button, the GET form writing `?city=red` and the prefix match against `Redmond` (lower-case input vs capitalised city). e2e because the behaviour is the form submission and enhanced navigation in the browser.

items.title: Opening `/stores?city=PORT` directly lists only AdventureWorks Portland
covers: AC3
Inputs: City kept in URL as ?city=<text>
Inputs: ignoring letter case
Outputs: opening that URL shows the same filtered list
items.reason: AC3 covers the deep link (the filter read from the query string on first load, not from a form post) and case-insensitivity with an all-upper-case value. e2e because it is a direct browser navigation to the URL.

items.title: Searching for `Boston` shows `No stores in "Boston".` and no store
covers: AC4
Outputs: No stores in "<text>". and no store
items.reason: AC4 defines the empty result: an exact message string and no store rows. A wrong quote style, missing period or a list still rendered would break it. e2e through the form, as the AC describes a search.

items.title: Clearing City on `/stores?city=red` and pressing Find stores lists all four stores again
covers: AC5
Inputs: Empty shows every store
items.reason: AC5 protects the reset path: an empty `City` (submitted as `?city=`) must not be treated as a filter that matches nothing. e2e because it starts from a filtered URL and submits the form in the browser.

items.title: City text with surrounding spaces (`den` with two spaces before and after) lists only AdventureWorks Denver
covers: Inputs: ignoring surrounding spaces
items.reason: The Inputs rule says the filter ignores surrounding spaces; without trimming, `den` with surrounding spaces would match nothing. No AC exercises it, so it needs its own case. e2e because the filter lives in the page component and there is no WebApp unit test project.

items.title: No-match message shows the typed text trimmed: `Boston` with two spaces before and after gives `No stores in "Boston".`
covers: Outputs: No stores in "<text>". (with the text as typed, trimmed)
items.reason: The output rule says the message echoes the text "as typed, trimmed"; an implementation that echoes the raw value would show the spaces inside the quotes. Separate from TC-STORE-1-05 because it checks the trimming of the echoed text, not the empty state itself.

items.title: A text that occurs inside a city but not at its start (`land`) matches no store
covers: Inputs: city starts with the text
items.reason: The rule is "starts with", not "contains": `land` is inside `Portland` but is not its prefix. A `Contains` implementation would wrongly list Portland. Opened via URL to keep the step to one action; the URL path is the same filter (AC3).

items.title: The whole city name `Seattle` (longest matching prefix) lists only AdventureWorks Seattle
covers: Inputs: city starts with the text (boundary: whole city name)
items.reason: Boundary just inside the prefix rule: the text equal to the full city still matches. Pairs with TC-STORE-1-11 (one character longer). e2e via the URL, as in AC3.

items.title: The text `Seattles` (one character past the city name) matches no store
covers: Inputs: city starts with the text (boundary: text longer than city)
items.reason: Boundary just outside the prefix rule: a text longer than any city cannot be its prefix. Catches an implementation that checks the reverse direction (text starts with city).

items.title: Opening `/stores?city=` lists all four stores
covers: Inputs: Empty shows every store
Inputs: Kept in the page URL as ?city=<text>
items.reason: An empty field is submitted as `?city=` (Inputs: empty shows every store). Opening that URL directly must not show `No stores in "".`. Separate from TC-STORE-1-06, which goes through the form.
